title: Market like a team of ten
description: Learn from what already worked, hear what people say about you, and turn one idea into content for every channel, with real data in front of you.
introduction: Marketing teams are small and the to-do list isn't. There's always one more report to pull, one more competitor to check, and one more post to write for a channel you forgot about.

Strawberry works inside your analytics, social accounts, CMS, and the live web, so it does the digging and the drafting with real numbers in front of it. It can make the images too. Think of it as the extra hands the team never got budget for.

blocks.text: Not sure where to start? Your companion can look at the work you have open and suggest the first thing worth handing over.

skill.context: Ask your companion to look at your work and suggest the first thing to hand over.

blocks.text: Point Strawberry at the last year of your posts. It finds the ones that did best, works out what they have in common, and turns that into a brief for the next ones. Your own history is better advice than any content playbook.

sections.title: Hear what people say about you

blocks.text: Reviews, Reddit threads, LinkedIn comments, and forum posts. Strawberry reads them in the browser and brings back a short report, or a deck in your brand, with a link to every quote. It's the fastest way to learn which words your customers actually use.

Pricing pages, changelogs, ads, and job posts say a lot about where a competitor is heading. Strawberry checks them, tells you what changed, and says what it means for you, not just how they're different.
Give Strawberry a talk, a launch, or a long post. It turns it into versions for LinkedIn, X, email, and the blog in your voice, with generated images where a stock photo would have gone.

sections.title: Find out why search traffic moved

blocks.text: Strawberry can work inside Search Console and your analytics while you're logged in, check the live search results, and come back with a short list of fixes in order of impact, with screenshots so you can see the evidence yourself.

items: Plan a campaign from what's already in your analytics and past launches.
Review last month and decide what to change, with the numbers pulled for you.
Build a list of high-fit accounts for a campaign.
Turn research into a beautiful deck in your brand.

blocks.text: Your brand voice, your audience notes, and what worked last quarter shouldn't live in one person's head. Save them with the team and every companion writes and researches the same way.
Put the weekly numbers and the competitor check on a Routine, and Monday starts with a short summary instead of four dashboards.
